standard.title: Write and read CVC words
standard.description: write consonant–vowel–consonant (CVC) words by representing sounds with the appropriate letters, and blend sounds associated with letters when reading CVC words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can name letters, produce letter sounds (AC9EFLY11), and segment and blend phonemes (AC9EFLY10). They have not yet been asked to connect phoneme-grapheme knowledge in both directions: encoding (writing) and decoding (reading) CVC words.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can write CVC words by encoding phonemes as letters, and read CVC words by blending the letter sounds — demonstrating bidirectional phoneme-grapheme correspondence at the CVC level.

nodes.label: Sounds can be written as letters
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can represent each phoneme in a CVC word with the correct letter when writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Write at least five CVC words correctly from dictation, representing each phoneme with the appropriate letter.
nodes.typical_width: Write CVC words across all short vowel sounds by representing each phoneme with the appropriate letter; spell common CVC patterns reliably.
wider: Write CVC words across all five short vowel sounds — ensuring the vowel discrimination is secure
Write CVC words in the context of real writing tasks — labelling drawings, completing simple sentences
Sort CVC words by vowel sound — building awareness of short vowel patterns
nodes.hinge_reason: CVC encoding is the prerequisite for the spelling strategy in LY13 — students who cannot reliably encode CVC words cannot extend phoneme-grapheme correspondence to unknown words. Encoding errors also propagate directly into the writing tasks in LY06.

response_modes.reason: CVC encoding must become reliable and accurate — encoding errors cascade directly into unintelligible writing. Practice across all short vowels is required before accuracy is secure.

success_criteria: Student correctly writes at least five CVC words, including words with different vowels.
Student represents each phoneme with the correct letter — not just onset and final consonant.

nodes.label: Letters can be blended into words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read CVC words by blending the sounds associated with the letters left to right.
nodes.minimum_width: Read at least five CVC words by blending letter sounds.
nodes.typical_width: Blend the sounds of CVC words when reading; apply blending to new CVC words not previously seen; read CVC words in the context of simple texts.
wider: Read CVC words in connected text — applying blending in the context of meaning-making
Read CVC words across a range of vowel patterns — not limited to familiar words
Identify CVC words in a familiar text and read them aloud — connecting letter-sound knowledge to reading fluency
nodes.hinge_reason: CVC decoding is the prerequisite for reading connected text in LY04 — students who cannot blend CVC words cannot apply phonic decoding to unknown words in authentic texts, and their reading remains dependent on memorisation.

response_modes.reason: Blending at the word level must become fluent — slow, halting blending interferes with comprehension. Accuracy first, then fluency across multiple CVC words.

success_criteria: Student reads at least five CVC words by blending, including unfamiliar words.
Student reads CVC words within a short decodable text rather than only in isolation.
